oneliner.t: Nonpartisan (independent) first-time candidate from Naknek — a Dena'ina Athabascan commercial salmon fisherman and retired Bristol Bay Borough School District superintendent (2013–2023) — who placed second in the Aug. 18, 2026 primary with 32.5% and is Begich's main challenger.

born.note: Both sources are his own questionnaire/pamphlet answers; no independent birth record found. Exact date not published.

hometown.t: Kokhanok (Iliamna Lake), Alaska; moved to Naknek as a teenager

profile.residence: Naknek, AK (temporarily living in Anchorage for the campaign)

upbringing.t: Born in Maryland and brought to Alaska as an infant; his pamphlet lists Kokhanok, on Iliamna Lake, as home from 1969 to 1984 before the family moved to Naknek, where he finished at Bristol Bay High School. He is Dena'ina Athabascan. He worked construction before earning a UAA education degree, taught (including six years at Floyd Dryden Middle School in Juneau), and moved into rural school administration. He has fished Bristol Bay commercially since childhood and owns a drift-gillnet permit and boat. He and his wife Diane have four children.

career.role: Commercial salmon fisherman (S03T Bristol Bay drift gillnet permit; F/V Vellamo)
Teacher (Naknek; Floyd Dryden Middle School, Juneau)
Student services director; principal of Igiugig School (2010–2012)
Superintendent (2023 Alaska Superintendent of the Year)
Co-owner (40% joint interest; listed as limited partner)
career.org: Bristol Bay Brailer LLC (marine textile manufacturing, Naknek)

platform.t: Lower costs for groceries, gas, child care and health care; supports extending ACA premium tax credits; opposes tariffs that raise prices.
Ban stock trading by members of Congress and their spouses.
Make billionaires and large corporations pay more; middle-class tax relief.
Opposes Pebble Mine; wants strict trawl bycatch limits and investment in salmon science and habitat.
Opposes Medicaid work requirements as red tape that would cut access.
Restore ICE funding to prior levels with more training and oversight, limits on masks and tactical gear, and judicial warrants for home entry.
Congress should reclaim its powers over war, spending, taxes and trade.
Should be safe, accessible and a decision between a woman and her doctor.
Continue Ukraine aid; condition aid to Israel on U.S. and international humanitarian law, withholding it if compliance can't be shown.
Says he has never been a registered Republican or Democrat and won't pick a House caucus ahead of time.

promises.t: Ban stock trading by members of Congress and their spouses.
Champion community schools and work to lower gas and grocery prices.
Will not commit to either party's caucus before the election.

record.t: Only his own answers (pamphlet; Beacon survey: Fort Meade) were found.
AASB (2022) describes him as an alumnus of the Bristol Bay Borough School District; UAA says he moved to Naknek as a sophomore.

claims.claim: Bachelor's in Education (secondary science), University of Alaska Anchorage.

record.t: UAA's own news office calls him a secondary education alumnus (degree year not given).
AASB (Oct. 2022) says he had been superintendent since 2013; ADN reports he retired from public education in 2023.

claims.claim: Named Alaska Superintendent of the Year (2023).

said.where: Beacon questionnaire bio; repeated in launch coverage

record.t: The Alaska Superintendents Association named him 2023 Alaska Superintendent of the Year (announced fall 2022).

claims.claim: Teacher 1998–2009; Lake and Peninsula student services director 2009–2013 and Igiugig principal 2010–2012.

record.t: UAA confirms six years teaching at Floyd Dryden Middle School in Juneau; Alaska Public Media confirms teaching in Naknek and Juneau and administration in Lake and Peninsula. Exact years not independently confirmed.

claims.claim: Commercial fisherman who owns a fishing boat in Bristol Bay (fishing since 1977).

record.t: His House disclosure lists a jointly owned S03T Bristol Bay drift-gillnet permit ($100K–$250K), two loans on the F/V Vellamo, and $244,049 gross fishing income in 2025. A Dec. 2025 campaign-style profile says he started fishing at 12, which would be about 1980–81, not 1977.
Disclosure shows a 40% joint (with spouse) interest ($15K–$50K) and lists him as a limited partner; his spouse draws income from it. Part-owner rather than sole owner.

claims.claim: Former board member and former board president of Paug-Vik Village Corporation.

record.t: His May 2026 candidate disclosure lists him as President of Paug-Vik Incorporated during the Jan. 2025–Apr. 2026 reporting period (no end date given); whether he has since left the post is not documented. His Beacon survey says 15 years on the board, 10 as president.

claims.claim: Members of Congress and their spouses reported over $600 million in stock-trading gains in 2025.

record.t: No source for the figure was given or found in this pass.

fec.src_note: pac_all = FEC 'other committee contributions' (not itemized here; Wikipedia lists union endorsements from the Alaska AFL-CIO, NEA, AFGE, flight attendants, carpenters and UA Local 367, but which committees gave was not confirmed). 'other' = $7,400 transfers from authorized committees + $2,230.54 offsets. Itemized individuals = 77% of receipts.
fec.quarters_note: Campaign figure, 'more than $780,000' from 4,500+ donors (Alaska Current); not an FEC figure.

support: Wheel Dog PAC (hybrid PAC; all IEs, candidate split not shown on FEC page)
Unnamed groups, combined (~$3M since Aug. primary)

fec.outside_note: ADN (Aug. 2026) says Wheel Dog PAC backs Hill and had spent more than $2M; a pro-Hill PAC (ADN does not say which) spent $50,000 countering a pro-Hafner text campaign, and Wheel Dog's texts urged voters to back 'the real Alaskan, not the guy in a NY prison.' Alaska Public Media (Oct. 2) reports roughly $3M from pro-Hill groups since the primary (groups not named; may overlap Wheel Dog). House Majority PAC reserved over $2.4M in Alaska ads in April but had not endorsed a challenger. Wikipedia's ADN headline (not opened) says a national Democratic group backed Hill in September.

money_flags_note: Not a clean finding. $62,050 in committee money could not be itemized, so business-PAC money can't be confirmed or ruled out (endorsing unions are not business PACs). Wheel Dog PAC's funders ($1.4M from other committees, $253,000 from individuals, $950,000 in 'other receipts') are not named on its FEC summary. No pro-Israel or other foreign-policy PAC money found.

superpac_donors.note: Receipts $2,622,253.54 thru 2026-07-29: individuals $253,000 (all itemized), other committees $1,400,000, other receipts $950,000.18; contributor names did not load.

note.t: Candidate report (covering Jan. 1, 2025–Apr. 15, 2026; signed May 15, 2026): assets valued at $119,006–$360,000, chiefly a joint Bristol Bay drift-gillnet permit ($100K–$250K), a 40% stake in Bristol Bay Brailer ($15K–$50K), small XRP and XLM crypto holdings, Silver Bay Seafoods and Bristol Bay Native Corp. shares, and a teacher-retirement pension (value undetermined). 2025 income: $244,049 gross from fishing, $81,778 pension, and his spouse's $48,181 from Bristol Bay Brailer. Liabilities $450,003–$1,000,000: a May 2025 commercial real-estate loan ($250K–$500K) and two loans on the F/V Vellamo. Homes don't have to be listed, so net worth isn't computed. The Anchorage Press reports he moved to Anchorage for the campaign and pays himself about $700 a week. No stock trades (candidate reports don't require PTRs).

research_notes: Primary Aug. 18, 2026: 53,008 votes (32.5%), second of 15. Raised $200,000 on his first day (Alaska Public Media). Endorsements (Wikipedia): Matt Schultz (after withdrawing July 17), former Gov. Tony Knowles, former Lt. Gov. Fran Ulmer, several state legislators, Dan Osborn, and unions including the Alaska AFL-CIO, NEA, AFGE and Carpenters. He cites the late Rep. Don Young as a model. Polls listed by Wikipedia (all Democratic-sponsored) show Begich ahead by 4–10 points in August. The 'prospectus' PDF is unsigned and appears to be a campaign or allied document; it is cited only for his own claims. Photo not retrieved.
